title: Grammar: Modal Verbs for Obligation, Permission, and Prohibition
grammarTip:
Модальные глаголы в юридическом и формальном письме:

ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬСТВО / ТРЕБОВАНИЕ:
shall → юридически обязателен: "The tenant shall pay rent by the 1st."
must → строгое требование: "All documents must be submitted."

РАЗРЕШЕНИЕ:
may → официальное разрешение: "The committee may adjourn the meeting."
can → менее формально: "You can request an extension."

РЕКОМЕНДАЦИЯ:
should → рекомендуется: "Applicants should submit all required documents."
ought to → менее частый формальный вариант

⚠️ Юридическое "shall" ≠ обычное "will":
"I shall be there." (формальное обещание)
"All parties shall comply." (юридическое обязательство)

grammarTable.subject: must
grammarTable.short: it is required / it is forbidden
grammarTable.example: "All defendants must be informed of the charges against them." / "Courts must not be politically influenced."

grammarTable.subject: have to / need to
grammarTable.example: "Witnesses have to tell the truth under oath." / "Lawyers need to register with the bar."

grammarTable.subject: should / ought to
grammarTable.example: "Judges should declare conflicts of interest." / "Citizens ought to be aware of their rights."

grammarTable.subject: may
grammarTable.example: "The accused may remain silent." / "Evidence may not be withheld from the defence."

grammarTable.subject: can / cannot
grammarTable.short: is able to / is not able to (legally)
grammarTable.example: "Anyone can access the court records." / "You cannot be convicted without evidence."

grammarTable.subject: be allowed to / be permitted to
grammarTable.example: "Defendants are allowed to consult a lawyer." / "Juveniles are not permitted to appear in adult courts."

grammarExtra.title: Must vs Have To: Strong vs External Obligation

rows.form: Must = internal/strong obligation (often moral or legal principle)
rows.example: "Governments must protect their citizens' rights." (a moral/legal imperative)

rows.form: Have to = external obligation (imposed by rules or authority)
rows.example: "Lawyers have to pay annual registration fees." (an external rule)

rows.form: Must not = strong prohibition (a legal or moral ban)
rows.example: "Judges must not accept gifts from parties in a case." (categorically forbidden)

rows.form: Don't have to = no obligation (but it is permitted)
rows.example: "Suspects don't have to answer police questions." (they have the right to remain silent)

grammarExtra.title: May, Can, Be Allowed To: Permission in Formal Contexts

rows.form: May (formal permission)
rows.example: "Any citizen may request access to public court records."

rows.form: May not (formal prohibition)
rows.example: "The jury may not communicate with either party during the trial."

rows.form: Be allowed to (less formal permission)
rows.example: "Defendants are allowed to have a lawyer present during questioning."

rows.form: Cannot (strong prohibition — not possible legally)
rows.example: "A person cannot be tried twice for the same crime." (legal principle)

grammarExtra.title: Should and Ought To: Moral and Professional Obligation

rows.form: Should = recommendation or expected behaviour
rows.example: "Witnesses should answer questions truthfully and completely."

rows.form: Ought to = moral duty (slightly more formal than should)
rows.example: "Prosecutors ought to disclose all relevant evidence to the defence."

rows.form: Should have + pp = past obligation not fulfilled (regret/criticism)
rows.example: "The judge should have recused himself — he had a conflict of interest."

rows.form: Ought to have + pp = same as should have (slightly more formal)
rows.example: "The evidence ought to have been disclosed earlier."

grammarExtra.title: Formal Legal Language: Shall, Be Required To, Be Obliged To

rows.form: Shall (in legal documents) = mandatory obligation (formal written law)
rows.example: "All parties shall be notified of the hearing date." (in a statute or contract)

rows.form: Be required to + infinitive = external obligation
rows.example: "Employers are required to provide written contracts." / "States are required to provide legal aid."

rows.form: Be obliged to + infinitive = obligated to do
rows.example: "Lawyers are obliged to maintain client confidentiality." (professional duty)

rows.form: Be prohibited from + gerund = cannot do this
rows.example: "Police are prohibited from questioning suspects without a lawyer present."

grammarExtra.title: Common Errors with Modal Verbs in Legal Contexts

rows.form: ❌ Suspects must not answer questions. (= they are forbidden)
rows.example: ✅ Suspects don't have to answer questions. (= they have the right to remain silent, but may speak if they wish)

rows.form: ❌ The judge should recuse himself last week.
rows.example: ✅ The judge should have recused himself last week. (past unfulfilled obligation = should + have + pp)

rows.form: ❌ Lawyers are allowed from revealing client information.
rows.example: ✅ Lawyers are prohibited from revealing client information. (prohibited from + gerund)

rows.form: ❌ All citizens can to vote.
rows.example: ✅ All citizens can vote. / All citizens are allowed to vote. (no "to" after "can")

exercises.text: "The accused ___ be presumed innocent until proven guilty." (strong legal principle)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for formal permission.
exercises.text: "The defendant ___ remain silent when questioned by police."
"Police ___ (= are forbidden from) question a suspect without a lawyer present." (prohibition)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for no obligation.
exercises.text: "Suspects ___ answer police questions — they have the right to remain silent."
exercises.hint: "Don't have to" = no obligation (but they may if they choose)

exercises.text: "Lawyers ___ (= are obligated to) maintain client confidentiality at all times." (professional duty)
exercises.correct: are obliged to / are required to

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for past unfulfilled obligation.
exercises.text: "The judge ___ recused himself — he had a clear conflict of interest."
exercises.hint: "Should have + pp" = past obligation not fulfilled (criticism/regret)

exercises.instruction: Complete with a formal legal modal.
exercises.text: "All parties ___ (= are required in law) submit written evidence before the hearing date." (legal document style)
exercises.hint: "Shall" in legal documents = mandatory obligation (written law)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for strong prohibition.
exercises.text: "Jurors ___ discuss the case with anyone outside the court during the trial."
exercises.hint: "Must not" = strong prohibition — it is categorically forbidden

exercises.text: "Citizens ___ (= have the right to) vote in all public elections once they reach legal age."
exercises.correct: are entitled to / are allowed to
exercises.hint: "Are entitled to / allowed to + infinitive" = have the right to

exercises.instruction: Which expresses a recommendation, not a strong obligation?
opts: "Courts must not interfere with jury deliberations."
"States shall provide legal aid to those who cannot afford it."

exercises.text: "Evidence ___ (= is forbidden from being) withheld from the defence." (legal prohibition — passive)
exercises.correct: may not be / must not be
exercises.hint: "May not be withheld" or "must not be withheld" = formal passive prohibition

exercises.text: "The witness ___ lie under oath — perjury is a serious criminal offence."
"Lawyers cannot reveal their clients' communications to the police." → Lawyers ___ revealing their clients' communications to the police.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for a past obligation that was not fulfilled.
exercises.text: "The evidence ___ submitted earlier — the delay caused serious harm to the claimant."
exercises.hint: "Should have been + pp" = past obligation not fulfilled (passive)

exercises.text: "The court ___ notify both parties of the hearing date at least 14 days in advance."
"Defendants are allowed from speaking to their lawyer before questioning."

questions.text: "All suspects ___ be treated equally under the law — regardless of social status." (legal principle)
"The accused ___ (= has the legal right to) know the specific charges against them."
questions.correct: is entitled to / is allowed to
questions.hint: "Is entitled to + infinitive" = has the legal right to

questions.text: "Suspects ___ answer questions — they have the right to remain silent." (no obligation)
questions.hint: "Don't have to" = no obligation, they may speak if they wish

questions.text: "The judge ___ accepted gifts from either party — it is a fundamental breach of judicial ethics."
questions.hint: "Should not have + pp" = past action that was done but shouldn't have been

questions.text: "Police ___ (= are formally forbidden from) using excessive force during arrest." (formal passive prohibition)
questions.correct: are prohibited from using / must not use
questions.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" or "must not use" = formal prohibition

questions.text: "Must not" and "don't have to" have the same meaning in legal English.
questions.hint: "Must not" = forbidden; "don't have to" = no obligation but permitted

questions.text: "In the contract: All parties ___ submit claims within 30 days of the incident." (legal document style)
questions.hint: "Shall" in legal documents = formal mandatory obligation

questions.text: "Evidence ___ not be withheld from the defence." (formal legal prohibition — passive)
questions.hint: "May not be withheld" = formal legal prohibition (passive)

questions.text: "Lawyers ___ (= are legally required to) report suspicions of money laundering to the authorities."
questions.correct: are required to / are obliged to
questions.hint: "Are required to / obliged to + infinitive" = legal/professional obligation

questions.text: "Prosecutors ___ disclosed the evidence earlier — the late disclosure was a serious procedural error."
questions.hint: "Should have + pp" = past obligation not fulfilled

questions.text: "Citizens ___ (= have the right to) appeal against decisions made by lower courts."
questions.correct: are entitled to / are allowed to
questions.hint: "Are entitled to" = have the legal right to

questions.text: Which sentence expresses a recommendation, not a legal requirement?
opts: "Judges should declare any conflicts of interest."
questions.correct: "Judges should declare any conflicts of interest."
